reliability_summary: Dry dual-clutch PowerShift DPS6 design flaw; shudder, clutch and TCM failures often from 30-50k km.
Above-average 1.2 Kappa engine; possible timing-chain rattle after 100-150k km; city-car segment.

The Hyundai i20 (PB generation, 2012-2015) with the 1.4L 100hp engine and 4-speed torque-converter automatic is generally well regarded: the i20 line has repeatedly placed in the top 10 of What Car?'s reliability surveys and won Auto Bild's TÜV Report 2019 best-compact-car award with only 3% serious-defect rate. This specific combo uses a conventional planetary automatic (not the later dual-clutch robotic gearbox found in some Hyundai/Kia models), which avoids the DCT-related jerking/clutch-wear complaints seen in 2014-2016 models. The main known issue across 2012-2015 i20s is AC compressor failure/refrigerant leaks around 50,000-70,000km; some owners also report delayed or jerky shifts starting around 60,000-80,000km, fixable via fluid change or valve-body service. CarComplaints shows relatively few filed complaints for this generation, suggesting either low reported-issue volume or low sample size. Israeli sources describe the model as generally reliable but flag checking the cooling system for overheating risk. Confidence is medium: survey data is strong but mostly UK/German-market, and Israeli-specific long-term data on this exact engine/gearbox combo is thin. Sources: What Car? reliability surveys, Auto Bild TÜV Report 2019, CarComplaints.com, AUTODOC BLOG, motor-center.co.il, auto.co.il.

reliability_summary: Overall below-average reliability, capped by a known transmission design flaw: for this generation/engine (2011-2014 1.2 69hp), the 'automatic' is the Dualogic robotized-manual, which owner forums (FiatForum, Fiat500 Forum, Honest John) consistently report for jerky shifts, unwanted neutral engagement, slipping gears and actuator/hydraulic failures needing costly repair. The 1.2 FIRE engine itself is simple and durable, commonly reaching 250k+ km with basic maintenance (timing belt, oil leaks at gaskets/seals being the main wear items), so the engine is not the concern. General reliability surveys put the Fiat 500 below segment average (JD Power ~70/100, RepairPal 18/21, US News 12/13 subcompacts), consistent with the gearbox complaints rather than contradicting them. Confidence is medium: the Dualogic identification is inferred from the model year/engine/market (not explicitly confirmed on this specific listing), and no Israel-specific forum threads on this exact combo were found, though general sources agree closely.

reliability_summary: Overall the Spark's 1.4L 4-speed automatic is a mid-pack, not a top-tier, choice: US complaint trackers list 2017 among the Spark's worse years for transmission gripes (delayed/rough 1-2 shifts, occasional shudder around 50-55mph), while the same sources note the 2016-2022 generation was notably quieter on serious defects than the rough 2013-2015 years. GM issued a free TCM reprogramming recall (N192268880) for 2016-2018 Sparks to fix a software issue where a faulty TCM memory bank could hide fault codes - a software fix, not a hardware failure, and low-cost/low-risk. Typical transmission repair costs cited for the Spark line run $1,500-3,000 in the rare failure cases, though only a handful of formal complaints exist for the 2017 model specifically. Israeli owner forums (CarsForum, FXP) show mixed but mostly unremarkable experiences, with some noting Korean-built GM small cars hold up well for roughly 5 years before wear issues accumulate. Evidence is thin/conflicting between 'worst years' lists and 'quieter generation' claims, so confidence is medium; sources: CarComplaints.com, KBB, RepairPal, NHTSA recall N192268880, carsforum.co.il, fxp.co.il.
